name: SSRF → IMDSv1 → Stolen EC2 Role Credentials
description: An image-resize endpoint trusts a user-supplied URL and fetches it server-side. Attacker passes http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ec2-app-role and the app cheerfully returns AWS temp credentials. They use them from a residential IP to enumerate S3.
reasoning: EC2 with IMDSv1 still allowed (legacy AMI). The simulation models the moment the role's credentials start being used from outside the VPC — CloudTrail picks up an unfamiliar source IP for a known principal.

nodes.label: image-resize-svc
nodes.notes: Fetches user-supplied URL. Hop limit not enforced; IMDSv1 enabled on the AMI.

nodes.label: ec2-imdsv1
nodes.notes: 169.254.169.254 endpoint. Returns temp creds for ec2-app-role.

narrative.text: Steady image-resize traffic; ~70 req/s, normal user-uploaded URLs.
Single source IP starts probing /resize?src=http://169.254.169.254/... patterns.
Successful response: AccessKeyId/SecretAccessKey/Token returned in the resize service's body.
Stolen creds used from residential IP 87.93.x.x against s3:ListObjects on every bucket.
Role's session policies revoked; AMI flipped to IMDSv2-required and rolled out.
Forensics: 4 buckets enumerated, no objects pulled (deny-by-default policy held).
Steady state. SCP added to forbid IMDSv1 going forward.
